questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Cross Product of Two Vectors Whose Angle Is a Non-Special Angle
questions.problem: The vector $u$ has magnitude $6$, the vector $v$ has magnitude $7,$ the angle between $u$ and $v$ is ${134}^{∘}$ and $n$ is the unit vector that points in the direction of $u\times v.$ Find $u\times v$ in terms of $n.$ Round your final answer to one decimal place where appropriate.
questions.worked_solution:
We use the formula for the cross product and obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}u\times v & =|u|\cdot |v|\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \cdot n \\  & =6\cdot 7\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{134}^{∘}\cdot n \\  & =42\cdot (0.719\,33…)\cdot n \\  & =(30.212\,27…)\cdot n \\  & ≈30.2n.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Cross Product of Two Parallel Vectors
questions.problem: The vector $u$ has magnitude $2,$ the vector $v$ has magnitude $5,$ and the angle between the vectors is ${0}^{∘}.$ What is $u\times v?$
questions.worked_solution:
Suppose $u$ and $v$ are nonzero vectors. Then, $u\times v=0$ if and only if $u∥v.$

Since the angle between $u$ and $v$ is ${0}^{∘},$ our vectors must be parallel. 

Therefore, $u\times v=0.$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Cross Product of Two Parallel Vectors
questions.problem: The vector $v$ has magnitude $12,$ the vector $w$ has magnitude $10,$ and the angle between the vectors is ${0}^{∘}.$ What is $v\times w?$
questions.worked_solution:
Suppose $a$ and $b$ are nonzero vectors. Then, $a\times b=0$ if and only if $a∥b.$

Since the angle between $v$ and $w$ is ${0}^{∘},$ our vectors must be parallel. 

Therefore, $v\times w=0.$
